questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place where I could experience a different culture than the one of my home university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was able to get in contact with the Mobility Office and introduction days were offered at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I knew a friend whose house I could move into

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be careful with scamming. Make sure you see the place and get a contract before you pay any money.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It could be a little difficult to get in contact with the Mobility office, but overall they were helpful. As soon as the registration opened, classes would be filled up very fast (within hours), so be ready for whenever it opens

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write emails and set up meetings – it was not possible to talk to anyone in person without a scheduled meeting

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Relatively, the courses were filled up quickly

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to sign up as soon as possible – the available courses in English are filled up very quickly

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Differed from class to class, but most had good and interesting academic content

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some what different – you are expected to turn in assignments and give presentations throughout a course, and attendance is taken in most classes, and all of this will have influence on your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Philosophy of Emotions, English Literature, and Discourse Analysis

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Peninsular Kingdoms of the Middle Ages, European Geography, Globalization and Gender, Gender Studies, Anthropology, African Cultural Studies, Historiography of Art, and Introduction to Digital Humanities 
OBS = my host university offer terms and not semesters, so the courses listed in this box where spread out over two terms

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the courses that I took was very interesting, I especially enjoyed Philosophy of Emotions, English Literature, Globalization and Gender, Historiography of Art, and African Cultural Studies

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Water is not really drinkable, so you must buy that, but luckily it's cheap

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was relatively cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Parties, discussion clubs, and seminars – however, most of these are in Catalan or Spanish

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The different seminars given in English at the University were very interesting

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of the city, visit Costa Brava, Sitges, Garraf, and other surrounding areas

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy – it is a city with many open (and international) people

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be active in approaching people – Catalan people can (without generalizing too much) be a little closed off in the beginning

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Of course the language, but other than that not many challenging but rather fun and refreshing differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A more relaxed mindset and attitude towards most parts of everyday life. A very big 'staying outside of your house' culture like going out for dinner, coffee etc

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check up on all deadlines especially during enrollment for courses, remember to check Aula Global (their version of Absalon) regularly – that's where most professors send out information during a course, and enjoy!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The red velvet muffin in the cafeteria is amazing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely getting to know people from a different culture and try and live their academic life for a while.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not many great challenges, but just overall adaption to a different way of attending university (assignments during course, attendance etc)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
